name: Small bus (SORCE class)
description: A small, light spacecraft body. Cheap and quick to build, but it can only carry and power a little, and its radio is slow.

source.title: NASA Earth Science Reference Handbook (2006)
source.detail: Key SORCE Facts and instrument facts, PDF p. 232-235. Bus mass = 315 kg spacecraft minus 66.6 kg of instruments flown.

name: Medium bus (EO-1 class)
description: A mid-sized spacecraft body with a fast X-band radio. Room for one or two modest instruments.

source.title: NASA Earth Science Reference Handbook (2006)
source.detail: Key EO-1 Facts and instrument facts, PDF p. 142-144. Bus mass = 529 kg spacecraft minus 100.5 kg of instruments (ALI and LAC). NASA Earth Observing-1, WARP section: 48 Gbit storage.

name: Large bus (Landsat 7 class)
description: A big, strong spacecraft body that can carry and power a heavy instrument and send data home very fast. Costly and slow to build.

source.title: NASA Earth Science Reference Handbook (2006)
source.detail: Key Landsat 7 Facts and Key ETM+ Facts, PDF p. 188-190. Bus mass = 1982 kg spacecraft minus the 425 kg ETM+. Downlink is one of its three 150 Mbps links. PDF p. 190: 380 Gbit recorder.
